```sql
-- name: top_customers
-- owner: sales
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
-- Customers ranked by revenue, with their most recent order. Only customers
-- whose last order falls inside the window are listed; this is what the
-- account managers asked for ("who was active this quarter").
WITH tenant_orders AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           o.total_cents,
           o.created_at
      FROM orders o
      JOIN customers c
        ON c.id = o.customer_id
       AND c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
agg AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           sum(total_cents)  AS revenue,
           count(*)          AS order_count,
           max(created_at)   AS last_order_at
      FROM tenant_orders
     GROUP BY customer_id
),
active AS (
    SELECT *
      FROM agg
     WHERE last_order_at >= %(from)s
       AND last_order_at <  %(to)s
)
SELECT c.id,
       c.email,
       c.company,
       c.country_code,
       a.revenue,
       a.order_count,
       a.last_order_at
  FROM active a
  JOIN customers c
    ON c.id = a.customer_id
 ORDER BY a.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De herschreven query filtert op tenant vóór de aggregatie, zodat de MATERIALIZED-CTE niet meer alle orders van alle tenants hoeft te scannen. Het aggregeren gebeurt in één pass per klant, en `max(created_at)` levert dezelfde waarde als de DISTINCT ON-variant. Bij gelijke omzet blijft de volgorde niet-deterministisch, net als in het origineel.
